questions.q: Before dbt, what did a transformation like building a customer summary table typically look like?
options: An untested SQL script or stored procedure someone ran by hand or on a schedule
It could not be done at all without dbt
It was always a Python script, never SQL
It required a dedicated data engineering team by law
questions.explain: Before dbt, that logic was usually a hand-run or scheduled SQL script with no tests, no docs, and no guaranteed run order.

questions.q: In the before/after example, what is the one concrete line that changes in the SQL itself?
options: A hardcoded table name becomes a ref() call
All SELECT statements become INSERT statements
The SQL has to be rewritten in Python
Every column name must be capitalized
questions.explain: The transformation logic barely changes — the hardcoded table name is replaced with a ref() call to another model.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four problems this lesson attributes to raw, untested SQL scripts?
options: They automatically generate a BI dashboard
No tests — a broken assumption fails silently
No documentation of what a column means
No version history of who changed what
questions.explain: Raw scripts lack tests, documentation, dependency awareness, and version history — they never generated dashboards on their own, dbt or not.

questions.q: What does dbt build automatically from every ref() call in a project?
options: A dependency graph that determines the correct run order
A billing invoice for warehouse usage
A list of every employee's login history
A backup of the raw source tables
questions.explain: dbt reads every ref() across the project to build the dependency graph and run models in the right order automatically.

questions.q: Why does 'one untested script' being manageable not mean 'a few hundred of them' will be?
options: Without something like dbt, nobody can tell which of hundreds of interdependent scripts ran successfully or in what order
SQL scripts stop working entirely after 100 files
Warehouses have a hard limit of 50 scripts
It actually does scale fine without any tooling
questions.explain: A handful of scripts can be tracked mentally; hundreds of interdependent, untested scripts with no shared ordering or history become unmanageable without dbt-style tooling.
